_:
scn — the storefront for Dr. Michael Kekong's eight PDF blueprints. SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes only)
+ Tailwind v4 + adapter-cloudflare (Workers). Repo root ~/i/scn, deploying to scn.apexlinks.org.
pnpm only, never npm/npx. It is HIS storefront: his name, his WhatsApp, his Paystack account.

=== THE CONCEPT — every step serves it ===
The site is an unexposed photographic plate. Nothing here is a secret; it is just unlit. The visitor's
cursor is the light: text develops where they look. Every book cover ships underexposed and develops on
hover, with a scan line passing over it. Paying develops the plate for good — the download appears.
Motion is EXPOSURE, never sliding: things fade up while un-blurring, slowly, with mass. One loud thing
(the light) in a very quiet room; everything else is disciplined and still.

=== DESIGN TOKENS (defined in src/app.css, only ever used as Tailwind classes) ===
plate #08090c ground · plate-2 #0e1015 raised · plate-3 #14171d hairlines and edges
bone #e9e4da developed text · lume #cbe7ea cold scan light · ember #e6a45e warm light, used ONLY for
prices and buy actions · ash #7b818a meta and mono labels
font-display Instrument Serif (headlines, book titles) · font-sans Instrument Sans (body)
font-mono JetBrains Mono (uppercase tracked labels: "PLATE 03 · 111 PAGES · PDF")
ease-expose cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) for reveals · ease-state cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) for hovers
text-mega / text-huge / text-big are clamp() display sizes; body text stays >= 16px.

=== HOUSE RULES (from ~/AGENTS.md — non-negotiable) ===
- snake_case for every variable and function. Type keys, JSON request keys and page-load return keys
  are SINGLE LETTERS (i, t, s, c, p, a, h, d, l, w, m, e, f, o, u, k, r).
- Svelte 5 runes only: $props $state $derived $effect. NEVER `export let`.
- No comments in code. Clean names and structure instead.
- No variable that is used once.
- All UI text lowercase. Book titles keep their own capitalisation.
- Tailwind utilities only. NO inline style= and NO <style> blocks, with exactly two exceptions, both
  of which pass a live number into CSS and nothing else: the stagger index (style="--i:{n}") and the
  scan sweep. The pointer light sets --mx/--my from JS via node.style.setProperty, not from markup.
- Forms submit on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter only, never plain Enter. Use `ctrl_enter` from $lib/actions.
- Secrets are read only through `$env/dynamic/private` and unwrapped with `get_secret` from $lib/secret.
- Local env vars live in .env. NEVER create .dev.vars.
- NEVER put `wrangler types` in the build script. `pnpm gen` runs it by hand when bindings change.
- Never start the dev server.

=== QUALITY FLOOR — never traded for looks ===
prefers-reduced-motion is respected everywhere (each reveal has a static, legible equivalent).
Animate only transform / opacity / filter. Layout works down to 360px. Visible keyboard focus.
Semantic HTML and real alt text. Nothing essential is EVER hidden behind the light — it reveals
atmosphere only; nav, book titles, prices and buttons are always fully legible. If JS never runs the
page still reads and the whole catalogue is still browsable and linkable.

=== COMMANDS ===
pnpm check = svelte-check · pnpm test = vitest once · pnpm build = vite build · pnpm gen = wrangler types
Every gate starts with `bash plan/verify_tests.sh`, which byte-compares each staged test already placed.
Copy staged tests with the exact `cp` the step gives. Never type a test out. Never "fix" one of its
imports. Make a red test pass by changing the implementation.

=== THE PRODUCT FILES ===
The eight source PDFs live in ~/Downloads (mapped to slugs in plan/assets/prep_covers.py). They are
what customers pay for: they are never committed to the repo and never placed in static/. They live in
a private Cloudflare R2 bucket named `scn`, keyed `<slug>.pdf`, bound to the Worker as `F`.

=== DELIVERY MODEL (no database, no login, no email) ===
checkout POSTs {e,i} -> paystack_init with our own reference and metadata {i} -> paystack popup ->
paystack redirects to /r?reference=... -> /r verifies the reference against Paystack, reads the item id
back out of the metadata, and lists a download link per book -> /d/<reference>/<slug> verifies the same
reference again and streams the object out of R2. Known ceiling, accepted on purpose: the receipt link
is shareable, and every download costs one Paystack verify call.

fonts.s:
Self-host the five type faces. Run exactly:

    bash plan/assets/get_fonts.sh

That script (already written, do not modify it) pulls the latin subset woff2 for Instrument Serif
regular + italic, Instrument Sans 400 + 500, and JetBrains Mono 400 from Google Fonts and writes them
to static/fonts/ as InstrumentSerif-Regular.woff2, InstrumentSerif-Italic.woff2,
InstrumentSans-Regular.woff2, InstrumentSans-Medium.woff2, JetBrainsMono-Regular.woff2.

Nothing else in this step. Do not add a <link> to fonts.googleapis.com anywhere — the site self-hosts,
and app.css declares the @font-face rules in the next step but one.

If the download fails because the machine has no network, block the step; do not substitute other
fonts and do not fall back to a CDN.

covers.s:
Render the eight book covers as "developing plates", plus the social preview image. Run exactly:

    python3 plan/assets/prep_covers.py

That script (already written, do not modify it) opens each source PDF in ~/Downloads, lifts the
embedded cover image out of page 1, contains the whole cover inside a 1100x1100 plate-black frame,
desaturates slightly, and multiplies a radial vignette over it so every title ends up sitting in the
same pool of light. It writes static/covers/<slug>.webp for all eight slugs
(killer-collection, killer-reset, ai-cashflow, ai-cashflow-2, silent-poverty, digital-skill, jamb, waec)
and static/og.jpg, a 1200x630 grid of all eight dimmed toward the edges.

It needs pypdf, pillow and numpy. If any is missing:  pip install --user pypdf pillow numpy

The covers deliberately ship at full brightness in the file — the underexposure is a CSS filter that
hover removes, so the "develop" effect is real and reversible. Do not pre-dim the images.

Do not copy any PDF into static/. Do not commit anything from ~/Downloads.

CREATE src/routes/+page.ts with exactly this content: export const prerender = true; Why the field is rendered twice: the dim copy is always there at 6% so the hero never looks empty and the text is still selectable and present in the DOM for search engines; the lit copy is the same markup masked to a soft circle that follows --mx/--my. Do not "simplify" this to one copy with a changing opacity; the mask is the effect. The whisper positions live in the class string (`left-[2%] top-[6%]`) rather than an inline style so Tailwind can see them and the no-inline-style rule holds. The crowded ones carry `hidden sm:block` so they never collide with the headline on a 360px screen.

r2_files.s:
Put the eight product PDFs in the private R2 bucket the Worker reads from. These files are the product;
they never enter git and never enter static/.

1. Create the bucket (idempotent — if it already exists, that error is fine, move on):

    pnpm exec wrangler r2 bucket create scn

2. Upload the eight PDFs under the exact keys the catalogue expects — <slug>.pdf. Run this verbatim:

    cd ~/Downloads && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/killer-collection.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "THE SILENT KILLER COLLECTION.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/killer-reset.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "THE SILENT KILLER RESET.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/ai-cashflow.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "AI CASHFLOW BLUEPRINT.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/ai-cashflow-2.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "AI CASHFLOW BLUEPRINT 2.0.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/silent-poverty.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "SILENT POVERTY.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/digital-skill.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "The Digital Skill Nobody is Teaching in School.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/jamb.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "JAMB MASTERY BLUEPRINT WITH UPDATED 2026 AND 2027 SYLLABUS.pdf" && \
    pnpm --dir ~/i/scn exec wrangler r2 object put scn/waec.pdf --remote --content-type application/pdf --file "WAEC A+ BLUEPRINT.pdf" ; cd ~/i/scn

3. Confirm all eight landed:

    pnpm exec wrangler r2 bucket list && pnpm exec wrangler r2 object get scn/waec.pdf --remote --file /tmp/scn_check.pdf && ls -l /tmp/scn_check.pdf && rm /tmp/scn_check.pdf

Do NOT make the bucket public and do NOT attach a public r2.dev url. The only way in is /d/<ref>/<slug>,
which re-verifies the Paystack reference on every request.

If wrangler is not authenticated (`pnpm exec wrangler whoami` fails), block this step rather than
guessing at credentials.

deploy.s:
Ship it to scn.apexlinks.org.

1. EDIT wrangler.jsonc. It currently contains exactly this block:

	"r2_buckets": [
		{
			"binding": "F",
			"bucket_name": "scn"
		}
	],

Add the custom domain route directly above it:

	"routes": [
		{
			"pattern": "scn.apexlinks.org",
			"custom_domain": true
		}
	],
	"r2_buckets": [
		{
			"binding": "F",
			"bucket_name": "scn"
		}
	],

2. Set the live Paystack secret key on the Worker. TEMPORARY — user approved using the live key from ~/i/e4 until Dr. Michael Kekong opens his own
Paystack account (planned same day). Rotate this secret when his key arrives. It must
never be committed, never go in wrangler.jsonc, and never go in .env:

    pnpm exec wrangler secret put PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY

   Paste the sk_live_... key when prompted. If you do not have it, block this step — do not deploy with
   a test key on a live domain.

3. Build and deploy:

    pnpm build && pnpm exec wrangler deploy

4. Point the Paystack dashboard's callback at the site. In the Paystack dashboard, Settings → API Keys
   & Webhooks, set the callback url to https://scn.apexlinks.org/r . The checkout also passes
   callback_url per transaction, so this is a belt-and-braces default for the hosted payment page.

5. Confirm the live site actually serves the catalogue and does NOT leak the products:

    curl -sf https://scn.apexlinks.org | grep -qF 'the things nobody tells you'
    curl -sf https://scn.apexlinks.org/b/waec | grep -qF 'WAEC A+ Blueprint'
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://scn.apexlinks.org/d/not-a-reference/waec

   The last one must print 403 or 502 — anything that starts with 2 means the download gate is open and
   the step is not done.

DNS: the custom_domain route makes Cloudflare create the scn CNAME on apexlinks.org itself. If the zone
is not on the same Cloudflare account as this Worker, block the step rather than adding records by hand.
deploy.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && pnpm check && pnpm build && grep -qF 'custom_domain' wrangler.jsonc && curl -sf --max-time 30 https://scn.apexlinks.org | grep -qF 'the things nobody tells you' && curl -sf --max-time 30 https://scn.apexlinks.org/b/waec | grep -qF 'WAEC A+ Blueprint' && curl -sf --max-time 30 https://scn.apexlinks.org/sitemap.xml | grep -qF '/b/jamb' && test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 30 https://scn.apexlinks.org/d/not-a-reference/waec)" != 200
